primary.key: Maruts, accept this thousandfold allotment of household sacrifice and household treasure.
primary.s: Midway through a long hymn to the Maruts, the singer turns from their splendour to their share of the home rite; Sāyaṇa, on 7.56.14, reads the single portion as a thousandfold, since an oblation spreads as far as the deity desires.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 7.56.14, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.५६, revision 403392 (2024)

basis.words: एकं भागं सहस्रियमिति कथमाह । तथा च श्रूयते … यावदेका देवता कामयते यावदेका तावदाहुतिः प्रथते न हि तदस्ति यत्तावदेव स्याद्यावज्जुहोति
basis.gloss: How can it call one portion thousandfold? For so it is heard [Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.2.6.4]: as much as the one deity desires, so far the one oblation spreads; for there is nothing that stays only as much as one offers.

standby.key: Sleep mother, let the father sleep, sleep dog and master of the house. Let all the kinsmen sleep, sleep all the people who are round about.
standby.s: The hymn turns from the guardian of the dwelling to a barking son of Saramā and on to a lullaby; Sāyaṇa, introduction to 7.55, following the Bṛhaddevatā, takes it as the charm by which Vasiṣṭha, entering Varuṇa’s house by night, hushed the dog and household.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, introduction to 7.55, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.५५, revision 189875 (2019)

basis.words: बृहद्देवतायां यदुक्तं तदिह लिख्यते … वरुणस्य गृहान् रात्रौ वसिष्ठः स्वप्नमाचरन् । प्रविवेशाथ तं तत्र श्वा नदन्नभ्यवर्तत । क्रन्दन्तं सारमेयं स धावन्तं दष्टुमुद्यतम् ॥ यदर्जुनेति च द्वाभ्यां सान्त्वयित्वा ह्यसूषुपत् । एवं प्रस्वापयामास जनमन्यं च वारुणम्
basis.gloss: What is said in the Bṛhaddevatā is written here: Vasiṣṭha, seeking sleep, entered Varuṇa’s house by night; there a dog came at him, barking. That howling son of Saramā, running at him and ready to bite, he soothed with the two verses beginning ‘yad arjuna’ and put to sleep; in the same way he put the rest of Varuṇa’s household to sleep.
